proposals.before: Prince Yong Cunmei, a son of the Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong's third younger brother, received his title in Tongguang 3.
proposals.after: Prince of Yong (邕) Cunmei, a son of the Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong's third younger brother, received his title in Tongguang 3.
proposals.reason: 邕王 is a different fief character from 永王; English 'Prince Yong' conflates the two titles.

proposals.before: Congrong then nominated Vice Minister of Justice Liu Zan as his tutor and Hanlin Academician Cui Ruan as chief administrator of the marshal's headquarters.
proposals.after: Congrong then nominated Vice Minister of Justice Liu Zan as his tutor and Hanlin Academician Cui Zhuo as chief administrator of the marshal's headquarters.
proposals.reason: 崔棁 is Cui Zhuo; 'Ruan' is a wrong reading of 棁.

proposals.before: Congrong then memorialized for Vice Minister of Justice Liu Zan as prince tutor and for Hanlin Academician Cui Ruan as chief administrator of the marshal's headquarters.
proposals.after: Congrong then memorialized for Vice Minister of Justice Liu Zan as prince tutor and for Hanlin Academician Cui Zhuo as chief administrator of the marshal's headquarters.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 棁 as Ruan in the literal field.

proposals.before: Congrong was displeased. Withdrawing, he told his attendants, "I am given the marshal's command, yet my choice of staff is blocked—and no explanation of the emperor's intent is offered."
proposals.after: Congrong was displeased. Withdrawing, he told his attendants, "Having been given the marshal's charge, yet my request for staff is blocked, and the imperial intent has not been explained."
proposals.reason: Source Chinese writes 衣榮 (corruption of 從榮); idiomatic already names Congrong correctly, but the second clause is awkward and obscures 未諭製旨.

decisions.after: Prince of Yong Cunmei, a son of the Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong's third younger brother, received his title in Tongguang 3.
decisions.reason: Focus unit titles him 邕王存美; 'Prince Yong' under-renders the noble title. 'Prince of Yong' is the correct English form, but the proposed parenthetical Chinese character cannot appear in the English field.
Focus unit names 崔棁; 棁 is Zhuo, not Ruan. Cui Zhuo corrects a real personal-name error and leaves the rest of the idiomatic intact.
The same 崔棁 governs the literal field; Ruan is an unsupported reading of 棁, and Cui Zhuo restores the correct name.
Idiomatic already correctly identifies 衣榮 as Congrong and accurately renders 既付以元帥之任, 阻予請僚佐, and 未諭製旨. The proposed rewrite is stylistic and yields an incomplete English sentence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 既付以元帥之任，而阻予請僚佐，又未諭製旨也
